text: PD Biomarker Cascade — NVP-BEZ235 (Dual PI3K/mTOR Inhibitor), McMillin et al., Cancer Res 2009;69:5835-42 |  |  |  |  |  |

Source: MM.1S and panel of multiple myeloma (MM) cell lines, primary MM patient samples, MM.1S xenograft mice. All figures/panels in the main text (Figs 1-6); Supplementary Figs S1-S7 are cited but NOT included in the uploaded PDF. |  |  |  |  |  |
Tier | Tier Name | Biological Meaning | Key Biomarkers (this paper) | Primary Figures | Data Type | Suggested PD Model Class

1 | Target Modulation | Direct pathway inhibition at the drug's two targets (PI3K and mTOR); most proximal, fastest-responding biomarker layer. | p-Akt(Ser473), p-Akt(Thr308), p-mTOR, p-p70S6K, p-GSK3α/β (total protein as loading reference) | Fig 2C, Fig 3C | Western blot, single dose (100 nM), time course 0-24h — qualitative/semi-quantitative (no densitometry reported) | Indirect-response (Kin/Kout) turnover model per phospho-node once dose-ranging blot data exists; currently only single-dose kinetics fittable

2 | Survival-Signaling Balance | Downstream node where the cell's fate is decided — compensatory anti-apoptotic signaling can blunt target modulation before it reaches cell death. | Bcl-2, Bad, Bcl-XL levels; genetic rescue by myr-Akt (no protection) vs Bcl-2 overexpression (partial protection) | Fig 2A, Fig 2B, Fig 2D | Fig 2A/B: quantitative dose-response (%survival vs nM, extractable curves); Fig 2D: western blot, qualitative | 4-parameter (sigmoidal) Emax model fit separately for parental vs Bcl-2-OE to estimate a 'protected-fraction' / Emax-shift parameter

3 | Transcriptional / Pathway Output | Distal genomic readout of sustained pathway inhibition — captures delayed, integrated pathway activity rather than instantaneous target occupancy. | 13 GSEA-style signatures: myc (x2 gene sets), high-risk MM, angiogenic, proteasome, undifferentiated hES, mouse ES, p53-downregulated, hedgehog, hTERT, IRF4, notch, ribosome | Fig 4 | Time-resolved (2,4,8,16,24h), quantitative average signal difference vs control with 95% CI — best time-course dataset in the paper | Transit-compartment or turnover model capturing signal-transduction delay from target modulation to transcriptional change; fit per-signature

4 | Cell-Death Execution | Commitment to and execution of apoptosis — the mechanistic bridge between pathway/transcriptional change and loss of viable tumor cells. | Annexin V+/PI+ fractions, cleaved PARP, cleaved caspase-3, (sub-G1 fraction — Suppl. Fig S4, not in this PDF) | Fig 3A, Fig 3B | Fig 3A: quantitative flow cytometry % per quadrant, time course; Fig 3B: western blot, qualitative band trend only | Delayed sigmoidal / Weibull onset model for %apoptotic vs time, anchored to the text's stated commitment window (<24h MM.1S, >24h MR20/OPM2)

5 | Tumor / Efficacy Endpoint | Disease-relevant outcome — the biomarker layer a QSP model is ultimately built to predict, plus the selectivity margin against normal tissue. | %survival (MTT/CellTiter-Glo) across 20 MM lines + IC50 table; 5 primary patient samples; stromal/hepatocyte/PBMC selectivity; tumor volume; overall survival; combination surfaces | Fig 1A-D, Fig 5A-C, Fig 6A-C | Fig 1A/B/C/D: quantitative dose-response (high quality, IC50 table given); Fig 5A/B: quantitative time-course + Kaplan-Meier; Fig 6: 3D response-surface, moderate extractability | Population Emax model across cell-line panel (virtual population seed); Simeoni-style tumor-growth-inhibition (TGI) model for Fig 5A; parametric survival model for Fig 5B; Bliss/Loewe additivity surface for Fig 6
